# [Intro](#intro)

***Note:** this guide is a work-in-progress.*

### [What’s this guide about?](#whats-this-guide-about)

It’s hard to say exactly what this guide is about. It’s easiest to say that it is primarily about verifying **multi-threaded concurrent code** in [Verus](https://github.com/verus-lang/verus), and in fact, we developed most of this framework with that goal in mind, but these techniques are actually useful for single-threaded code, too. We might also say that it’s about verifying **code that needs unsafe features** (especially raw pointers and unsafe cells), though again, there are plenty of use-cases where this does not apply.

The unifying theme for the above are programs that require some kind of **nontrivial ownership discipline**, where different objects that might be “owned independently” need to coordinate somehow. For example:

-   Locks need to manage ownership of some underlying resource between multiple clients.
-   Reference-counted smart pointers need to coordinate to agree on a reference-count.
-   Concurrent data structures (queues, hash tables, and so on) require their client threads to coordinate their access to the data structure.

This kind of nontrivial ownership can be implemented through Verus’s `tokenized_state_machine!` utility, and this utility will be the main tool we’ll learn how to use in this guide.

### [Who’s this guide for?](#whos-this-guide-for)

Read this if you’re interested in learning how to:

1.  Verify multi-threaded concurrent code in Verus.
2.  Verify code that requires “unsafe” code in unverified Rust (e.g., code with raw pointers or unsafe cells)

Or if you just want to know what any of these Verus features are for:

3.  Verus’s `state_machine!` or `tokenized_state_machine!` macros
4.  Verus’s `tracked` variable mode (“linear ghost state”).

This guide expects general familiarity with Verus, so readers unfamiliar with Verus should check out the general [Verus user guide](https://verus-lang.github.io/verus/guide/) first and become proficient at coding within its `spec`, `proof`, and `exec` modes, using `ghost` and `exec` variables.

### [Further Reading](#further-reading)

For a fully comprehensive account, please see [Verifying Concurrent Systems Code](https://www.andrew.cmu.edu/user/bparno/papers/hance_thesis.pdf).

93: /// Print declaration for the Instance type.
94: ///
95: /// From the user's perspective, this should just be an opaque, unforgeable token type
96: /// that serves as an identifier for a protocol instance and contains the constants
97: /// for the instance.
98: ///
99: /// Formally, this token should be derived in terms of a monoid derived from the state
100: /// machine state. (See `monoid-formalism.md`.) Since that formalism is not
101: /// implemented mechanically
102: /// in Verus, we instead make the state itself a field. This is kind of meaningless, but it
103: /// serves as a placeholder and does result in the necessary dependency edge between this
104: /// struct and the type struct. The fields are private, so they shouldn't matter to the user.
105: ///
106: /// Another thing is that we need the `Instance` struct to have the correct Send/Sync traits.
107: /// (All the other token types will then inherit those traits. The Senc/Synd traits of
108: /// the Instance should depend on the Sync/Send traits of the storage types.
109: /// In particular, the Instance should be Sync+Send iff the storage types are all Sync+Send.
110: /// Otherwise, the Instance type should have neither.
111: /// Initially, this rule might seem a little extra-restrictive, but we need this restriction
112: /// because if it is possible for the instance to interact with another thread at all, it
113: /// could conceivably do arbitrary withdraw/deposits (thus 'sending' the storage objects
114: /// to the other thread) or arbitrary guards (thus 'syncing' the storage objects to the
115: /// other thread). Due to the flexibility of the guard protocol, this could theoretically
116: /// happen regardless of whether the instance/tokens are synced or sent to the other thread.
117: // TODO make sure that the Instance/tokens don't inherit !Sync or !Send negative-instances
118: // from the other fields where it doesn't matter. (Completeness issue)
119: fn instance_struct_stream(sm: &SM) -> TokenStream {
120:     let insttype = inst_type_name(&sm.name);
121:     let self_ty = get_self_ty(sm);
122:     let gen = &sm.generics;
123:     let attrs = &sm.attrs;
124: 
125:     let storage_types = get_storage_type_tuple(sm);
126: 
127:     return quote_vstd! { vstd =>
128:         #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, verifier::proof)]
129:         #[allow(non_camel_case_types)]
130:         #(#attrs)*
131:         pub struct #insttype #gen {
132:             // This is not marked external_body, but the fields are private, so the
133:             // user should not be able to do illegal things with this type from outside
134:             // the module created by the macro.
135:             // For example, this prevents the user from constructing an instance.
136:             // However, since it's not marked external_body,
137:             // Verus will still look at the fields when doing its type hierarchy analysis.
138: 
139:             #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, verifier::spec)] send_sync: #vstd::state_machine_internal::SyncSendIfSyncSend<#storage_types>,
140:             #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, verifier::spec)] state: ::core::option::Option<#vstd::prelude::Ghost<#self_ty>>,
141:             #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, verifier::spec)] location: #vstd::prelude::int,
142:         }
143:     };
144: }
145: 
146: /// If the SM has storage types T1, T2, ...
147: /// this returns the tuple type (T1, T2, ...).
148: /// Uses the "inner" type (e.g., the X in Option<X>, not Option<X> itself)
149: fn get_storage_type_tuple(sm: &SM) -> Type {
150:     let types: Vec<Type> = sm
151:         .fields
152:         .iter()
153:         .filter_map(
154:             |field| if field.stype.is_storage() { Some(stored_object_type(field)) } else { None },
155:         )
156:         .collect();
157:     Type::Verbatim(quote! { (#(#types),*) })
158: }

160: /// Add a `clone()` method to the Instance type (or any other type which is cloneable).
161: /// This is safe, because the Instance object effectively just represents
162: ///
163: ///   * the fact that the protocol exists, and has been initialized
164: ///   * any constants associated to the protocol
165: ///
166: /// TODO it would be even better to add a Copy instance as well; however, this
167: /// currently runs into Verus limitations with deriving instances.
168: fn trusted_clone() -> TokenStream {
169:     return quote_vstd! { vstd =>
170:         #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost_body)]
171:         #[verus::internal(verus_macro)]
172:         #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, verifier::proof)]
173:         #[verifier::external_body] /* vattr */
174:         #[verifier::returns(proof)] /* vattr */
175:         pub fn clone(#[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, verifier::proof)] &self) -> Self {
176:             ensures(|s: Self| #vstd::prelude::equal(*self, s));
177:             ::core::unimplemented!();
178:         }
179:     };
180: }

182: fn trusted_copy(self_ty: &Type, generics: &Option<Generics>) -> TokenStream {
183:     let impl_decl_clone = impl_decl_stream_for(self_ty, generics, quote! { ::core::clone::Clone });
184:     let impl_decl_copy = impl_decl_stream_for(self_ty, generics, quote! { ::core::marker::Copy });
185:     return quote! {
186:         // It shouldn't be possible to call this (you'd need an exec-mode object)
187:         // but we need to implement it so we can implement Copy.
188:         // Our other 'clone' function should override this, which makes it difficult
189:         // to accidentally call this.
190: 
191:         #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, verus::internal(verus_macro))]
192:         #impl_decl_clone {
193:             #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, verifier::external_body)] /* vattr */
194:             fn clone(&self) -> Self {
195:                 ::core::unimplemented!();
196:             }
197:         }
198: 
199:         #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, verus::internal(verus_macro))]
200:         #impl_decl_copy { }
201:     };
202: }

511: /// Primary method to build an exchange method for a given transition.
512: ///
513: /// To build an exchange method, we need to collect 4 key pieces
514: /// of information:
515: ///
516: ///  * input arguments (may include spec & proof tokens)
517: ///  * outputs (may include spec & proof tokens)
518: ///  * pre-conditions (mostly follow from 'require' statements)
519: ///  * post-conditions (mostly follow from 'update' and 'assert' statements)
520: ///
521: /// When possible, we use &mut arguments (i.e., if a given token is
522: /// both an input and an output).
523: pub fn exchange_stream(
524:     bundle: &SMBundle,
525:     tr: &Transition,
526:     safety_condition_lemmas: &HashMap<String, Ident>,
527: ) -> parse::Result<TokenStream> {
528:     let sm = &bundle.sm;
529: 
530:     let is_init = tr.kind == TransitionKind::Init;
531: 
532:     let mut ident_to_field = HashMap::new();
533: 
534:     // Initialize the `params` field of the `Ctxt` object. We'll fill this up
535:     // later; for now, just create an entry with an empty Vec for each relevant field.
536:     let mut params = HashMap::new();
537:     for field in &sm.fields {
538:         ident_to_field.insert(field.name.to_string(), field.clone());
539: 
540:         if !is_init {
541:             match &field.stype {
542:                 ShardableType::Multiset(_)
543:                 | ShardableType::Option(_)
544:                 | ShardableType::Map(_, _)
545:                 | ShardableType::IMap(_, _)
546:                 | ShardableType::PersistentOption(_)
547:                 | ShardableType::PersistentMap(_, _)
548:                 | ShardableType::PersistentIMap(_, _)
549:                 | ShardableType::Count
550:                 | ShardableType::PersistentCount
551:                 | ShardableType::Bool
552:                 | ShardableType::PersistentBool
553:                 | ShardableType::Set(_)
554:                 | ShardableType::ISet(_)
555:                 | ShardableType::PersistentSet(_)
556:                 | ShardableType::PersistentISet(_)
557:                 | ShardableType::StorageOption(_)
558:                 | ShardableType::StorageMap(_, _)
559:                 | ShardableType::StorageIMap(_, _) => {
560:                     params.insert(field.name.to_string(), Vec::new());
561:                 }
562:                 ShardableType::Variable(_)
563:                 | ShardableType::Constant(_)
564:                 | ShardableType::NotTokenized(_) => {}
565:             }
566:         }
567:     }
568: 
569:     let mut ctxt = Ctxt {
570:         fields_read: HashSet::new(),
571:         fields_written: HashSet::new(),
572:         fields_read_birds_eye: HashSet::new(),
573:         params: params,
574:         requires: Vec::new(),
575:         ensures: Vec::new(),
576:         ident_to_field,
577:         is_init: is_init,
578:         sm: bundle.sm.clone(),
579:         fresh_num_counter: 0,
580:     };
581: 
582:     let mut tr = tr.clone();
583: 
584:     check_unsupported_updates(&tr.body)?;
585:     check_ordering_remove_have_add(sm, &tr.body)?;
586: 
587:     // Potentially remove steps that won't be useful.
588:     // We want to do this before `find_all_accesses` below, since this step may potentially
589:     // remove field accesses that we would like to ignore.
590:     // For example, suppose the user writes `update(foo, pre.bar)` where `foo` is
591:     // NotTokenized. In that case, we want to make sure that we _don't_ process
592:     // pre.bar as a requirement to have `bar` as an input token.
593:     tr.body = prune_irrelevant_ops(&ctxt, tr.body);
594: 
595:     // compute `ctxt.fields_written`, which is used to determine the output tokens
596:     determine_outputs(&mut ctxt, &tr.body)?;
597: 
598:     // Determine which fields are read (e.g., `pre.foo`) and in what context those
599:     // fields are read.
600: 
601:     let mut errors = Vec::new();
602:     let (fields_read, fields_read_birds_eye) =
603:         find_all_accesses(&mut tr.body, &mut errors, &ctxt.ident_to_field);
604:     combine_errors_or_ok(errors)?;
605: 
606:     ctxt.fields_read = fields_read;
607:     ctxt.fields_read_birds_eye = fields_read_birds_eye;
608: 
609:     // translate the expressions in the TransitionStmt so that
610:     // where they previously referred to fields like `pre.foo`,
611:     // they now refer to the field that comes from an input.
612:     // Also simplifies away SpecialOps.
613: 
614:     let mut errors = Vec::new();
615:     translate_transition(&mut ctxt, &mut tr.body, &mut errors)?;
616:     combine_errors_or_ok(errors)?;
617: 
618:     // translate the (new) TransitionStmt into expressions that
619:     // can be used as pre-conditions and post-conditions
620:     // This fills up `ctxt.requires` and `ctxt.ensures`.
621:     exchange_collect(&mut ctxt, &tr.body, Vec::new())?;
622: 
623:     // For our purposes here, a 'property' is just a special case of a normal transition,
624:     // but 'init' transitions need to be handled differently.
625:     // For the most part, there are two key differences between init and transition/readonly/property.
626:     //
627:     //   * An 'init' returns an arbitrary new Instance object, whereas a normal transition
628:     //     takes an Instance as input.
629:     //   * An 'init' will always return tokens for every field that has tokens,
630:     //     and take no tokens as input (except for external 'storage' tokens).
631:     //     A normal transition takes tokens as input only as is necessary.
632:     //
633:     // Generally speaking, the input parameters are going to look like:
634:     //    (instance as the 'self' argument)?    (present if not init)
635:     //    (spec transition params,)*            (parameters to the transition)
636:     //    (proof token params,)*                (if init, only includes storage tokens;
637:     //                                           otherwise, includes storage tokens AND
638:     //                                           tokens of this instance)
639: 
640:     let mut in_params: Vec<TokenStream> = Vec::new();
641:     let mut out_params: Vec<(TokenStream, TokenStream, Mode)> = Vec::new();
642: 
643:     // First, we create a parameter for the Instance, either an input or output parameter
644:     // as appropriate.
645: 
646:     if ctxt.is_init {
647:         let itn = inst_type(sm);
648:         out_params.push((quote! { instance }, quote! { #itn }, Mode::Tracked));
649:     } else {
650:         in_params.push(quote! { tracked &self });
651:     }
652: 
653:     // Take the transition parameters (the normal parameters defined in the transition)
654:     // and make them input parameters (spec-mode) to the corresponding exchange method.
655: 
656:     for param in &tr.params {
657:         let id = &param.name;
658:         let ty = &param.ty;
659:         in_params.push(quote! { #id: #ty });
660:     }
661: 
662:     // We need some pre/post conditions that the input/output
663:     // tokens are all of the correct Instance.
664:     // We will fill these in as we go. (Note these might not contain all instance-related
665:     // conditions; for collection types, the pre- and post-conditions are more complicated
666:     // and in that case, some instance-related conditions might go in with the
667:     // `ctxt.requires` or `ctxt.ensures`).
668: 
669:     let mut inst_eq_reqs = Vec::new();
670:     let mut inst_eq_enss = Vec::new();
671: 
672:     // Whether or not to mark all borrows with a lifetime parameter 'a
673:     // We need to do this if there is any borrow in an out param
674:     // (which only happens for guards in 'readonly' transitions).
675:     let use_explicit_lifetime = ctxt.get_explicit_lifetime();
676: 
677:     for field in &sm.fields {
678:         // the 'init' case is different enough from the other two that we
679:         // handle it completely separately
680: 
681:         if ctxt.is_init {
682:             // For 'init', we start with a few special cases.
683:             // For a NotTokenized field, there's nothing to do. No token to output,
684:             // and no postcondition about it.
685: 
686:             match &field.stype {
687:                 ShardableType::NotTokenized(..) => {
688:                     continue;
689:                 }
690:                 _ => {}
691:             }
692: 
693:             // Sanity check some assumptions that should hold for any well-formed
694:             // 'init' routine. In particular, there should be no occurrences of `pre.field`
695:             // and every field should be written.
696: 
697:             assert!(!use_explicit_lifetime);
698:             assert!(ctxt.fields_written.contains(&field.name.to_string()));
699:             assert!(!ctxt.fields_read.contains(&field.name.to_string()));
700:             assert!(!ctxt.fields_read_birds_eye.contains(&field.name.to_string()));
701: 
702:             // Next case is the Constant type. We don't need to output a new token for it,
703:             // we just need to add a postcondition like `instance.field() == value`.
704: 
705:             match &field.stype {
706:                 ShardableType::Constant(_) => {
707:                     let e_opt = get_post_value_for_variable(&ctxt, &tr.body, field);
708:                     let e = e_opt.expect("get_post_value_for_variable");
709:                     let lhs = get_const_field_value(&ctxt, field, field.name.span());
710:                     ctxt.ensures.push(mk_eq(lhs.span(), &lhs, &e));
711:                     continue;
712:                 }
713:                 _ => {}
714:             }
715: 
716:             // Now everything else should fall into one of two buckets. We either need
717:             // to generate an input token or an output token.
718:             //
719:             // In most cases, we need to generate an output token param. This applies to
720:             // 'variable', naturally, but also 'option', 'multiset', etc.
721:             // And we need to generate a postconditions (an 'ensures') that the value of
722:             // the token is the value it was initialized to via the 'init' statement.
723:             //
724:             // For _storage_ type, we need to generate an _input_ token param.
725:             // The storage type comes externally from the system, so for example,
726:             // if the transition initializes the storage field to say, Some(x),
727:             // then the user needs to actually deposit 'x' in order to run
728:             // the initialization. Thus the Some(x) actually needs to come in
729:             // an input param.
730:             //
731:             // So in either case we:
732:             //  1. Determine type of the (input / output) token
733:             //  2. Determine the value the field is set to via the 'init' statement(s)
734:             //  3. Generate a (precondition / postcondition) that the token has
735:             //     the correct value.
736:             // Also note that in the non-storage (i.e., output) case, this includes
737:             // the conditions that the new tokens are all associated with the newly
738:             // generated Instance. But of course the input tokens have so such constraint.
739: 
740:             if let Some(init_input_token_type) = get_init_param_input_type(sm, &field) {
741:                 // Storage case, input token & precondition:
742: 
743:                 let arg_name = transition_arg_name(field);
744: 
745:                 add_token_param_in_out(
746:                     &ctxt,
747:                     &mut in_params,
748:                     &mut out_params,
749:                     &mut inst_eq_enss,
750:                     &mut inst_eq_reqs,
751:                     &arg_name,
752:                     &init_input_token_type,
753:                     InoutType::In,
754:                     false, // (don't) apply_instance_condition
755:                     false, // (don't) use_explicit_lifetime
756:                 );
757: 
758:                 let e_opt = get_post_value_for_variable(&ctxt, &tr.body, field);
759:                 let e = e_opt.expect("get_post_value_for_variable");
760: 
761:                 add_initialization_input_conditions(
762:                     field,
763:                     &mut ctxt.requires,
764:                     e,
765:                     Expr::Verbatim(quote! { #arg_name }),
766:                 );
767:             } else if let Some(init_output_token_type) = get_init_param_output_type(sm, &field) {
768:                 // Everything else case, output token & postcondition:
769: 
770:                 let arg_name = transition_arg_name(field);
771: 
772:                 add_token_param_in_out(
773:                     &ctxt,
774:                     &mut in_params,
775:                     &mut out_params,
776:                     &mut inst_eq_enss,
777:                     &mut inst_eq_reqs,
778:                     &arg_name,
779:                     &init_output_token_type,
780:                     InoutType::Out,
